status: AGENT-VERIFIED, NOT USER-VERIFIED, NOT EXACT. Conservative inner polygons that exclude the teal frame wire and the clips/tabs that protrude from it. Checked visually by Claude on corner, notch and edge zooms (figures/roi_*), and independently by Codex (parent) on 200 px corner zooms of the starting quadrilaterals. They deliberately sit a few pixels inside the wire, so a thin strip of barnacles next to the wire is excluded.
method: Start from the Codex-suggested quadrilateral (inner corners clear of the rounded wire junctions). region.wire_intrusions finds teal pixels inside it (G-R>25 and B-R>25), groups pieces within 15 px and pads each group's box by 8 px; region.notched_polygon cuts those boxes out as rectangular notches. Every corner, notch and edge was then inspected visually. Only visible frame geometry was used; no detector output, score or metric influenced any coordinate.
order: [x, y] original pixels, clockwise from top-left; quad = TL, TR, BR, BL. Polygon vertices on slanted sides are kept unrounded so the polygon never extends past the quad.

unseen_img1.png.use: Operational review ROI for unseen_img1 (replaces the earlier eye-read quadrilateral in corners_provisional.json, which touched the wire at rounded junctions and clips).
unseen_img1.png.refinement: None: the suggested quadrilateral cleared the wire on every corner and edge zoom (tightest straight-edge gap about 4-5 px, left and bottom-left edges); only the eight clip/tab notches were added.
